# AI-Lang

> A programming language written in natural language. You describe a system —
> its data, its rules, its boundaries — and the compiler emits Java, TypeScript,
> Python or Go, plus Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform or AWS. Compilation is
> deterministic: no model calls, no network, no randomness. The same source
> produces the same bytes.

The point is to move the conversation with a machine up one level. A design in
AI-Lang is a tenth the size of the code it produces, so it can be read, reviewed
and corrected before a single line is generated — and generating costs nothing,
because the compiler is a compiler.

Source files end in `.ail`. Start with the guide; it is complete on its own.

## Writing it

- [Agent guide](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the whole language in one file, written to be read by a model. Start here.
- [Language reference](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/docs/language-reference.md): every construct, exhaustively.
- [CRUD tutorial](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/docs/crud-tutorial.md): a working service from an empty directory.

## Worked sources

- [tasks.ail](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/examples/crud/tasks.ail): the five CRUD operations and nothing else.
- [orders.ail](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/examples/orders/orders.ail): aggregates, events, handlers, DTO projection.
- [subscriptions.ail](https://github.com/dscanavall11/ai-lang/blob/main/examples/billing/subscriptions.ail): adapters with config, scheduled work.

## Checking your work

Never hand back `.ail` you have not run. `ail check` type-checks and audits the
architecture, reporting exact spans and stable codes; `ail explain <code>`
explains any of them. `ail test` runs the scenarios the sources declare against
the IR in about a second — no code generated, no tokens spent.
